## Description
This PR is an alternative to https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/19226 as I didn't like much the fact we're adapting the iso9660 when it wasn't actually used to process the DVD. This fixes the detection logic instead.
I didn't test blu-ray playback as I don't have any way to do it (@DaVukovic if possible) but it should work™

## Motivation and Context
Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/18896
Restores optical DVD playback in Kodi

## How Has This Been Tested?
Tested in linux and windows (testbuild: http://mirrors.kodi.tv/test-builds/windows/win64/KodiSetup-20210303-60a8f395-PR15-merge-x64.exe)

## Screenshots (if appropriate):
See https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/19226

pr_comments:
Hey @howie-f, this doesn't fix your previous issue it just makes the dvd detection work without trying to open the video.ifo using the iso9660:// vfs. The path check keeps there for legacy reasons only.
We have previously concluded that VLC always open the raw optical device (/dev/dvd is passed to libdvdnav/read) whereas Kodi sometimes pass the root mount point (/mnt/mydvd) and according to some comment in the code it should work too (probably by luck :)). For me it always plays regardless of the path. In your VirtualBox passthrough setup the second one doesn't play but I highly doubt that's something on the Kodi side.
You should try to investigate why /dev/cdrom or /dev/dvd is not returned as the optical path in your setup by libcdio. I can't help much there, but please do not block this PR under the assumption your setup is something common :)
all good @enen92. that was just the user report, thought it may be of value. ofc not blocking, codewise i'm fine with this.

For me everything plays fine. CPU usage is at 20-24% with DVD playback and ~35% with BR-playback. So I can't complain in that regard. 

Tested with current Kodi master on Fedora and a 1050ti as a GPU

Can't comment on the code itself, unfortunately ;)
Thanks much for testing @DaVukovic. Glad to know BRs continue to play just fine

review_comments: would there ever be a case that a DVD wouldn't have this?

There is at least a case where the video_ts.ifo is in the root folder and not under video_ts: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/d6a4bc3f030d5e57e8e706ff5c759fa3e812eca0/xbmc/FileItem.cpp#L1829-L1832
Either way, this is used for dvd stacking / dvd folder storage on disk and not exactly to request playback from the optical drive (so a different code path). For this PR/fix if we manage to open the dvd with libdvdnav/read we can safely assume the item is a DVD.
